t: 3744 - Find Kth Character in Expanded String
o:
Each word expands so that its j-th character (0-indexed) repeats j+1 times; a word of length L therefore contributes L(L+1)/2 characters, and single spaces separate words contributing one character each. Since t can be astronomically larger than s (up to ~1.25e10 characters for a 1e5-length word), we cannot materialize t. Instead, accumulate per-word block lengths, locate which block (word or space) contains index k, then solve for the character position inside the word by finding the smallest j with (j+1)(j+2)/2 > local offset.

Example 1: k=0 lands in the first character block of 'hello' → 'h'. Example 2: 'hello' expands to 15 characters (1+2+3+4+5), so index 15 is the space between words.
k: Word of length L expands to L(L+1)/2 chars — prefix sums locate the owning word in O(#words)
Within a word, find smallest j with triangular(j+1) > offset; answer is word[j]
Never build t; its length can exceed 1e10

a.i: Split s into words. Walk through words accumulating expanded lengths (plus 1 per intervening space). When k falls inside a word's block, subtract the block start and advance j while the cumulative triangular count stays ≤ offset; the character is word[j].
s: Split s on spaces into words
For each word i with preceding space: if k == cursor, return space; cursor++
If k < cursor + L(L+1)/2: offset = k - cursor; find j minimal with (j+1)(j+2)/2 > offset; return word[j]; else cursor += L(L+1)/2
a.t: O(|s|) — splitting dominates; the inner search advances at most L steps total per query
a.sp: O(|s|) — the word list (avoidable with manual parsing)

w: The math here is triangular numbers; the inner search could also be a closed-form solve of j² + 3j + 2 > 2·off via sqrt, but a linear walk is already amortized fine. Pitfalls: forgetting the space characters between words (each occupies exactly one index), and 64-bit arithmetic — block lengths reach ~5e9, overflowing 32-bit types. Follow-up: answer many k queries — precompute the word prefix array once and binary-search each query in O(log #words).
